mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below its 5-year historical average indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance, which reduces the cost of capital and supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below its 5-year average, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A 1-month rise in unemployment rate above 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in non-farm payrolls and decrease in unemployment rate signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling does not produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, housing starts (HOUST) above 1300 thousand units signal overbuilding and potential market correction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1300 in late-cycle expansion regimes, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.0% signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A current industrial production level above its 5-year historical average indicates strong manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO is above its 5-year average, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and retail sales signals robust consumer demand and economic expansion, which boosts corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of HOUST and RSAFS rising does not produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), a decline in the unemployment rate signals improving labor market conditions, which increases consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is above 5.0% and declining, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
